articles.title: Geoffrey Hinton, el padrino de la IA: “No soy catastrofista. Creo que hay un 1% de posibilidades de que nos destruya”
articles.summary: El científico computacional y Premio Nobel de Física Geoffrey Hinton durante el Festival Starmus 2026 que se celebra este martes en el municipio de Arona en Tenerife. Hace años, cuando la gente preguntaba a Geoffrey Hinton por qué trabajaba con la inteligencia artificial, él repetía una frase de Oppenheimer, uno de los creadores de la bomba atómica: “Cuando ves algo grandioso, sigues adelante y lo llevas a cabo”. Ya no lo dice. Ahora se dedica a alertar sobre los peligros de continuar la carrera que él mismo empezó. Confiesa que, en parte, se arrepiente del trabajo al que ha dedicado una vida. Su reconversión de padrino de la IA a profeta de la catástrofe marcó un punto de inflexión en la industria. Sucedió en 2023, cuando abandonó su puesto como vicepresidente de Google entre advertencias funestas. Entonces, algunos vieron su reacción exagerada. Tres años después, muchos han seguido sus pasos. Viele Autofahrer:innen, die Android Auto für ihre Reisen nutzen, dürfen sich über zahlreiche Neuerungen freuen. Nicht nur, dass sich schon Android Auto 18 als großer Versionssprung am Horizont abzeichnet. Jetzt hat Google schon vorab ein KI-Upgrade für seinen Dienst ausgerollt. Die schlechte Nachricht für deutsche Autofahrer:innen, die sich auf KI-Features in Android Auto gefreut haben, vorweg: Wie Google im Kleingedruckten in der Ankündigung verrät, wird Personal Intelligence in allen Regionen außer der EU, der Schweiz, dem Vereinigten Königreich sowie Nigeria ausgerollt. Ob und wann die KI-Funktionen auch hierzulande nachgereicht werden, ist nicht bekannt.
Dementsprechend bleibt deutschen Android-Auto-User:innen vorerst nur zu hoffen, dass die Neuerungen auch in ihren Fahrzeugen landen. Sollte das zu einem späteren Zeitpunkt passieren, gibt es einige praktische Features durch Gemini und Personal Intelligence. articles.title: Inside Wikipedia’s Cleanup Effort Against AI Text
articles.summary:
Ellia Lebleu is a founding member of the WikiProject AI Cleanup, a volunteer effort launched in 2023 to find and remove AI-generated material from Wikipedia that breaks the website’s guidelines. When the cleanup began, AI writing was often betrayed by conspicuous clichés. Today, the project’s volunteers are developing tools to detect subtler forms of machine-generated content and debating AI’s role in the world’s most widely used encyclopedia.
When did you realize Wikipedia had a problem with AI-generated material?
Ellia Lebleu: It was around December 2023. A few other editors and I were chatting on Wikipedia’s Discord server, and we had all seen very strange articles with the same odd characteristics. They repeated phrases like “stands as a testament” or “rich cultural heritage.” They sometimes had conclusion sections, or sections called “Why is this important?” That was very typical of ChatGPT in 2023 and early 2024 but very odd for Wikipedia articles—and very easy to spot. Then I decided, let’s create an official project on Wikipedia so more people can deal with this.
Ellia Lebleu
Ellia Lebleu is a founding member of the WikiProject AI Cleanup. Lebleu is pursuing a Ph.D. in AI at the Inria Center of the University of Rennes, part of France’s national research institute for digital science and technology.

articles.title: How Commerce.com and Cloudflare are getting storefronts ready for AI agents
articles.summary:
How Commerce.com and Cloudflare are getting storefronts ready for AI agents
AI can write code and pass the bar exam, but it still struggles to buy a pair of shoes online.
That’s because websites were built for humans, not agents. Most agents that shop for someone today work from a site’s HTML — they look at the page, guess which button does what, click, and try again when they get it wrong. This process is slow, uses a lot of tokens, and something as seemingly innocuous as a theme change can break it.
Enter WebMCP: a browser standard from Google that gives AI agents structured tools on a page, like search_products. Instead of hunting for buttons, the agent calls the exact tool it needs directly, making shopping faster, cheaper, and far more reliable. Because WebMCP is still an experimental proposed browser standard in early preview, it’s currently available behind experimental Chrome flags (chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing), in Chrome Origin Trials, in some agentic browsers, and across developer environments like Cloudflare Kitesurf.
In August, we launched edge implementation of WebMCP in beta. Turn it on, and Cloudflare injects a tiny script at the edge to make those tools available automatically, without site owners writing a single line of code.
Commerce.com, a flexible commerce platform built for the age of AI, already uses Cloudflare to run their almost 100,000 domains. So when the preview came out, they asked: Can we turn this on for all of our stores at once?

Intel’s Ohio One US Manufacturing Push
The Ohio One project was announced in January 2022, with Intel saying production would start in 2025. The 1,000-acre site east of Columbus was part of a broader plan to expand domestic manufacturing capacity using state and federal funding alongside Intel’s capital investment.

articles.title: Starlink bridé en Ukraine : le gouvernement américain jette Elon Musk sous le bus
articles.summary:
Quelqu’un, vraisemblablement, ment. Interrogé par des journalistes en Inde ce mercredi 21 octobre, Marco Rubio, le secrétaire d’État américain, a lâché Elon Musk. Le responsable a en effet renvoyé au PDG de SpaceX la responsabilité de Starlink en Ukraine. Ce dernier disait de son côté qu’il fallait plutôt voir du côté de Washington.
« Starlink est une entreprise privée. Ils ont un contrat. Ils ont des conditions contractuelles sur la façon dont cette technologie peut être utilisée. Le point important est que nous ne pouvons pas dicter à une entreprise privée les décisions qu’elle prend ou ne prend pas », a déclaré Marco Rubio, ajoutant que, selon lui, la Maison-Blanche n’a pas son mot à dire.
« Ce que je peux vous dire avec certitude, c’est que ni le président des États-Unis, ni personne dans notre système, n’a jamais demandé que des modifications soient apportées à ce système. Et c’est ce que nous avons dit à plusieurs reprises », a-t-il ajouté. Ce serait donc Elon Musk qui aurait pris cette décision de ralentir l’emploi de Starlink en Ukraine.
Ici, Marco Rubio s’exprimait au lendemain d’une révélation du Wall Street Journal. Le journal avance qu’Elon Musk aurait lui-même donné l’ordre de brider Starshield, la version militaire de Starlink avec laquelle l’armée ukrainienne pilote ses drones. EmulateHeap kopiert die Eigenschaften des Speichermanagers von Windows 95 für neuere Systeme. Denn der hält gerade für Games Vorteile bereit, die spätere Inkarnationen von Windows nicht haben.

articles.title: Samsung’s 5K monitor has good gaming chops and a great price
articles.summary:
There are quite a few 5K monitors out there. Many of them are designed to appeal to Mac users who are looking for cheaper Studio Display alternatives without giving up the pixel-dense 218ppi screen. However, if you’re interested in hearing about one with gaming chops, Samsung’s 27-inch Odyssey G80HF seems like one of the best monitors out there to satisfy your niche, but respectable desires. Currently, you can grab this model for $599.99 at Amazon and B&H Photo, which beats its best price by $100.
Samsung’s 5K monitor has good gaming chops and a great price
Plus, save on gaming bundles including GTA VI, and grab an affordable five-port USB wall charger.
The G80HF supports two display modes with its Fast IPS panel: 5K at up to 180Hz refresh rate, or 1440p with up to a 360Hz refresh rate. Samsung touts Nvidia G-Sync compatibility as well as AMD FreeSync Premium to ensure the monitor’s refresh rate remains in lockstep with your GPU’s frame rate output. The monitor features a DisplayPort 2.1 port (just one, and Samsung doesn’t advertise its bandwidth), two HDMI 2.1 ports, and a USB hub for charging or connecting two USB-A 3.2 Gen 1 accessories.

The bridge to agent-scale Git infrastructure
We moved a copy of 99.99999% of GitHub’s repositories to Azure. Here’s how per-reference quorums will bring over the rest, and how object storage lets reads scale independently.
Over the past year, while Git traffic grew exponentially, 99.99999% of the Git repositories on GitHub began living in two places at once: our own data centers and Azure. The rest are among the busiest on the platform, and they’re held back by just one thing: a 25ms round trip.
In an earlier blog post, we laid out the two principles behind our next-generation storage architecture:
- Minimize coordination
- Decouple storage from compute
In this post, we’ll look at the immediate bridge between our old design and our new one. We’ll talk about how a change to the way our quorum serializes writes gets the busiest repositories into Azure, and how that same step opens the door to replicas that keep no persistent state of their own.
How we got here
The timing and shape of the move were driven by the agentic shift: rapidly growing traffic, a hard ceiling on the power capacity of our data centers and the surrounding geographical region, and physical supply chain constraints. Both organizations said that the bias occurred when the AI was prompted to code for an organization in a country of interest to the Chinese Communist Party (CCP). Hirundo has verified that on its own.
It instructed Alibaba’s Qwen3-Coder to build a web service that allows users to sign up, log in, and store secrets. The model built over 1,000 applications, and the test clearly showed the bias, Hirundo notes in a report shared with SecurityWeek ahead of publication.
“We ran every request through two models. The first is Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct as Alibaba ships it. The second is Hirundo’s Westernized Qwen3-Coder: the same model after we removed its CCP alignment from the weights with behavioral unlearning,” the company says.
Both were instructed to build apps for a US defense contractor, a Chinese defense contractor, and a Hong Kong democracy advocacy group.

Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
- Date:

- Source:

- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.

A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. TornadoVM, an open-source heterogeneous GPU programming framework for Java has reached version 7.3, a major milestone for the project.
InfoQ previously covered the project in December 2025 and in 2022.
TornadoVM automatically accelerates Java programs on multi-core CPUs and GPUs. Rather than replacing existing JVMs, it works alongside them and provides a rich GPU programming ecosystem in Java that you can use with any mainstream JDK distribution such as OpenJDK, Graalvm, Temurin, or Zulu.
It offloads Java code to hardware backends, manages memory between the Java heap and accelerators, and runs the resulting compute kernels. This makes it a useful building block for modern cloud and machine learning workloads.
During development, TornadoVM compiles the source Java code to OpenCL and Apple Metal backends. The idea is that you can develop locally on your laptop and use the hardware available locally, and then deploy into a server that has Nvidia GPUs, and achieve major performance improvements - a form of "Write Once, Run Anywhere" for modern ML workloads.
Version 7 brings several architectural changes. The backends now use the Foreign Function & Memory (FFM) API in place of the Java Native Interface (JNI). The experimental JVM Compiler Interface (JVMCI) dependency has also been removed. Was steckt hinter Dunkler Energie? Dies ist eines der großen Rätsel der Kosmologie. Die unsichtbare, hypothetische Form der Energie gilt als verantwortlich für die Ausdehnung des Universums, nachdem der erste Schub durch den Big Bang abgeklungen war.
Neuer Weg zum Verständnis von Dunkler Energie?
Direkt nachgewiesen werden konnte die Dunkle Energie, die fast 70 Prozent der Energiedichte des Universums ausmachen soll, noch nicht. Ein Forschungsteam könnte aber nun einen Weg gefunden haben, Dunkle Energie künftig besser zu verstehen.
Die Resultate ihrer Forschung haben die Wissenschaftler:innen in gleich zwei Papern vorgestellt, die beide in der Fachzeitschrift The Astrophysical Journal erschienen sind.

Die Forschenden haben mit dem Radioteleskop Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME) nach Spuren von kosmischem Wasserstoff gesucht. Genauer gesagt nach neutralem atomaren Wasserstoff, der nicht ionisiert und also elektrisch ungeladen ist.
Neutraler Wasserstoff sendet eine Radiostrahlung mit einer Wellenlänge von etwa 21 Zentimetern aus. Durch die Expansion des Universums wird die Strahlung auf dem Weg zur Erde zu niedrigeren Frequenzen verschoben.
Je stärker die Verzerrung im Vergleich zur ursprünglichen Wellenlänge ist, desto länger waren die Strahlen unterwegs. Daraus kann man ablesen, aus welcher Zeit die Signale stammen. …

articles.title: Introducing full transaction detection for Cloudflare WAF
articles.summary:
Introducing full transaction detection for Cloudflare WAF
Today, we are expanding our web application firewall (WAF) by adding two new capabilities: full transaction detections and response rules. Full transaction detections evaluate each HTTP request alongside its response to identify evidence of exploitation. It helps answer both "Does this request look malicious?" and "What happened when the application handled it?" Response rules can then block the origin’s response before it reaches the requester.
These are valuable protections because the latest frontier models are uncovering vulnerabilities buried deep in widely used software, giving defenders clarity on what to fix — and attackers new paths to exploit. The recent php2shell vulnerability shows the stakes: a flaw in a common software component can put applications across the Internet at risk. AI agents scanning for vulnerabilities can be extremely persistent, adapting payloads using feedback, and chaining vulnerabilities, credentials, and permissions. An application's response can reveal whether an attempt worked and give an attacker information that helps them go deeper.
Inspecting incoming requests remains essential for stopping recognizable attacks before they reach an application. But some threats become clear only when the request is considered alongside what the origin returns. A suspicious input followed by a response exposing sensitive information tells a different story from the same input followed by a rejecti…

The latest warnings reflect “the depth of strategic distrust between Beijing and Washington” even as U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping work hard to keep their personal relationship “warm and constructive,” said George Chen, partner and chair of digital practice at Washington-based The Asia Group consultancy.
The Homeland Security order, dating back to late July, also blocks civilian agencies from procuring DeepSeek products and services.
DeepSeek’s open-source models are widely available in countries including the United States, and are mostly free to use.

There’s no mention of any of the Personal Intelligence features that were announced yesterday for Gemini in Android Auto and cars with Google built-in, however, which enable the voice assistant to access user information from Google apps, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, YouTube, and Search. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.

Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.

articles.title: How NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture Secures and Governs AI Agent Workloads at Scale | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Autonomous agents can work for hours on complex tasks, accessing files, tools, the internet, and spawning other agents to collaborate with. Executing complex tasks over long time horizons leads to compounding risk: the agents may download code, build new tools, request additional privileges, and touch more of the underlying infrastructure.
The agents’ action paths are determined as they work and reason through the steps needed to complete their goals. As they interact with the tools and systems around them, they adapt their reasoning and behavior to achieve their task.
The adaptability of agents is what makes them so powerful, but they are goal-oriented and may not prioritize safety in pursuit of their objectives. In order for agents to work both autonomously and safely, we need to build environments that provide control and visibility in what the agent is doing.
An agent cannot govern itself. Security and governance belong in the infrastructure the agent operates in.
OpenShell provides deterministic governance outside of the agent’s reach
NVIDIA OpenShell is an open-source runtime to build the security and governance needed for agentic systems into the computing infrastructure. OpenShell defines and enforces which systems and data an agent can access, from files and internet services to systems that interact with physical devices.
It is the foundation of the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture for building safe AI agents. OpenShell treats agent workloads as untrusted thr…

Microsoft has released a public preview of dotnetup, a cross-platform toolchain manager that installs, updates, and removes .NET SDKs and runtimes inside the user's account rather than a system-managed directory. As reported on the .NET Blog, the tool was announced on October 15 by Chet Husk, program manager for the .NET SDK, and follows the model of rustup and nvm.
According to the documentation, commands and behavior may change between preview releases, and production machines should keep using the installers, package managers, or Visual Studio.
The design, as described in the announcement, tracks intent instead of versions. A developer asks for a channel such as latest, lts, preview, daily, a major like 10, a minor like 10.0, or a feature band like 10.0.1xx, and dotnetup resolves it to a release. Exact versions, as the post notes, stay pinned during updates.
Several requirements can share one managed installation, and the tool reads the nearest global.json so team builds stay deterministic. Furthermore, according to the docs, files live under the user's local data directory on Windows, macOS, and Linux, and dotnetup never writes to Program Files\dotnet or /usr/share/dotnet.
Installation uses a bootstrap script fetched from aka.ms with curl or irm. articles.title: NVIDIA cuDSS Now Generally Available to Accelerate Engineering and Scientific Simulations

Complex engineering feats — from advanced chips to aircraft to industrial systems —– depend on simulation to predict how designs will perform before they’re built. As designs become more complex, simulations take longer to run, increasing computing demands and limiting the number of ideas teams can test.
NVIDIA cuDSS accelerates solving large sparse systems — the math-heavy step that repeats throughout engineering and scientific simulations and often limits how many designs a team can test — by tapping into GPUs. This lets applications reduce time to results and increase simulation throughput, enabling end users to explore larger more realistic models, more accurate representations and a wider design space at a reduced cost.

articles.title: Inside NVIDIA Sentry: Secure AI Agents at Runtime | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
An AI agent can complete its assignment and still cross a security boundary. Recent incidents show that agents can circumvent security controls while using tools, credentials, and services to pursue their assigned goals. Monitoring and enforcement need to operate outside the agent’s reach so that it can’t alter or disable them.
NVIDIA Sentry is a security software framework that monitors AI agents and enforces policies governing their access to models, tools, and data. Part of the NVIDIA OpenShell reference architecture announced at GTC Berlin, it’s built on NVIDIA DOCA, runs on NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs, and provides host-isolated runtime protection for AI agents. NVIDIA Sentry validates that an agent operates according to its designed intent and within its defined operational boundaries.
Trusted even when host resources can’t be trusted, it controls the agent’s only path to the model, providing tamper-evident traceability of agent activity while enforcing granular security controls on agent access in silicon. In addition to inspecting agent communications, NVIDIA Sentry uses out-of-band observability to establish real-time situational awareness, continuously evaluating agents’ runtime security and behavior to validate their security and integrity.
This post explains how NVIDIA Sentry evaluates agent requests, detects threats, and enforces security policies independently of host software.

articles.title: Eliminating traffic deaths
articles.summary:
Eliminating traffic deaths
Deploying simple, proven methods for making our roads safer could save more than 1 million lives worldwide each year.
Every year, traffic crashes kill more than one million people, and they’re the leading cause of death for children and young adults. In the US, 100 people a day lose their lives this way, in many cases not on highways but on rural and local streets. “Traffic deaths are a leading cause of preventable death, yet we treat it like it’s inevitable,” says Leah Shahum, founder and director of the Vision Zero Network, a nonprofit focused on making streets less deadly.
The sticking points
The causes of a crash can be muddy. Drivers make mistakes like speeding or getting distracted, but infrastructure fails them too: Perhaps they were on a road built for speed and not safety, in a screen-filled vehicle, or at an intersection where pedestrians, cyclists, and other cars aren’t visible.
Cheap and proven traffic-calming opportunities abound—from using planters to tighten intersections to lowering speed limits—but government logjams and red tape can be speed bumps. “There’s so many moving parts,” says Laura Sandt of the University of North Carolina Highway Safety Research Center. “On the flip side, it shows that we have so many opportunities for injury prevention.”

These additions bring HTTP authentication and non-HTTP services such as databases and DNS under the same Kubernetes API used for web and gRPC traffic.
According to Vibert and Chaiehloudj, ExternalAuth allows an HTTPRoute to consult an external authorisation service before sending a request to an application. Depending on the response, the gateway can forward the request, redirect a user to a login page, or reject it. The authoriser can also pass identity headers to the application. TCPRoute and UDPRoute remove the need to fall back to LoadBalancer or NodePort Services for plain Layer 4 traffic.
ListenerSets address a separate ownership problem. articles.title: Browsers Block eMudhra Intermediate CAs Over Recoverable Private Keys

The private keys associated with eight intermediate certificates issued by Indian certificate authority (CA) eMudhra have been compromised, and root programs and trust stores have started blocking them.
The certificates were issued in April 2025, and some of the compromised keys could allow attackers to generate fraudulent certificates and impersonate any website.
On October 17, Mozilla and Google blocked the certificates in Firefox and Chrome. Apple and Microsoft blocked them on October 19 and October 20, respectively. Sectigo took revocation steps too, and Cloudflare patched its services.
eMudhra revoked the compromised certificates, and the issue was communicated to downstream trust stores.
“The private keys for these certificates were generated with insufficient randomness (i.e., weak cryptographic entropy), enabling anyone to forge trusted HTTPS certificates to impersonate any website against clients that have not yet removed trust in those CAs,” Google explains.
Although the certificates have been blocked and revoked, some clients may require software updates to ensure that the compromised intermediates are no longer trusted.
Mozilla’s Dennis Jackson has published a tool to check whether clients still trust the compromised certificates. He also explains that the private keys were incorrectly generated and could be retrieved from the certificates.

Choose amino acids for a 100-residue protein sequence and the number of possibilities exceeds the number of atoms in the observable universe. Somewhere in that space is a protein that opens a path to a new therapy. There are too many combinations to search exhaustively, so finding it depends on knowing where to look.
RFD4-Proteina, an NVIDIA BioNeMo open model co-developed with the Institute for Protein Design at the University of Washington’s School of Medicine, navigates that space using patterns learned from nature. articles.title: Getting old is hard. This age-tech housing aims to make it easier. | BetaKit

My grandmother was a commanding woman. In her 92 years, she raised three children and a grandchild, mostly by herself. She helped manage a series of successful restaurants and nightclubs; in her little spare time, she hiked and skied. She was decidedly capable.
But when I unexpectedly knocked on her door one autumn when I was 19, something was different: she asked me the same questions, different only in sentence structure, again and again.
What brought me to town?
Where was I going to school?
What was I doing in town?
What college was I enrolled in?
Over the years, she lost more of her faculties. Eventually, she left the stovetop on for so long that a steel pot melted into molten coagulant. That was the boiling point: a week later she moved in with my parents.
My grandmother’s experience was not abnormal. Like many seniors, she was caught between her desire to remain independent and the limitations of her advancing age; she didn’t want to leave her home, but could also no longer live safely on her own. With little money to afford in-home care, those years put untold pressure on my parents and left my grandmother in a sort of purgatory: she wasn’t independent, but she also didn’t have round-the-clock care.
If Calgary’s Garden Loft had been around back then, might things have been different?

articles.title: Solid-state batteries

Solid-state batteries
Batteries that swap liquid electrolytes for solid materials promise to charge faster, last longer, and (crucially) run cooler.
The rise of the lithium-ion battery, which powers everything from the smallest personal electronics to gargantuan energy storage systems, has been nothing short of revolutionary. But as anyone who’s boarded a plane in the last decade could tell you, storing and pumping out energy by moving charged lithium ions through a liquid electrolyte soup has its drawbacks, not least that the batteries have a troubling tendency to catch fire. Enter the solid-state battery, which swaps liquid for a solid ceramic or polymer, creating power packs that charge faster, last longer, cram more energy into smaller spaces, and (crucially) run cooler. A new generation of companies aim to bring such batteries to market, and if their bets pan out, the tech could substantially ease the shift away from fossil fuels.
The sticking points
Solid-state batteries have been “just a few years away” for more than a decade now. In laboratories, the technology works. But there have been challenges. In designs that pair the solid electrolyte with a lithium-metal anode (the side of the battery that releases electrons into an electrical circuit), needlelike filaments called dendrites tend to grow during charging, and they eventually push through the electrolyte and short the cell. articles.title: Distributed Spring Batch Without a Message Broker
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- Spring Batch can scale horizontally without a message broker by using the relational database it already requires as the coordination plane. It fits the small-to-medium clusters many teams run.
- The pattern solves the problems a broker otherwise handles for you: sizing work to the live node count, assigning per-execution master responsibility with no standing coordinator, and claiming partitions with compare-and-set writes so no partition is silently lost.
- Node failure is handled by heartbeats and a two-phase recovery. It marks a stale node as unreachable, then after a grace period window, removes it and reassigns its incomplete, transferable partitions.
- Correctness is an explicit contract. Transferable work runs at least once and must be idempotent; nontransferable work runs at most once and is failed rather than moved. A partition is never silently lost.
- Database coordination fits where operational simplicity and cost matter most. Its ceiling is database contention and past that point, at very large clusters or sub-second latency, a broker remains the better choice.
Introduction
Spring Batch has been the default framework for batch processing on the JVM for more than a decade. Jobs are built from steps, such as chunk-oriented readers, processors, and writers, with a metadata repository that makes runs restartable. For the nightly extract, transform, load (ETL), financial reconciliation, and data-validation workloads on a single machine, it is hard to …

Nvidia wants new AI capacity to show up at the data center fully built. At its GTC Berlin conference on Wednesday, the company introduced DSX POD, a reference design for shipping containers that partners fill with Vera Rubin racks, networking, and liquid cooling before they leave the factory.
Installing and wiring up racks in a conventional data center can take months, Nvidia says. But a DSX POD can be ready to deliver tokens in as few as 14 days, as long as the site already has the necessary power, cooling, and network connections (which are, to be fair, often bottlenecks, too).
The idea here is for data center operators to get to value faster, because, as Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang said in a statement, “An AI factory creates value when it starts producing tokens — not when construction is complete.”
What’s in the box
Each container holds seven Vera Rubin NVL72 racks, or 504 Rubin GPUs. Ian Buck, Nvidia’s vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing, said in a press briefing ahead of the announcement that a single unit packs about 10 million components and weighs around 28 metric tons.
The containers also come with roughly 20 kilometers of copper cabling and 17 kilometers of scale-out networking preinstalled and tested. Once a container arrives, crews set it in place, connect it to its neighbors, and run the final burn-in tests, Buck said.

articles.title: J’ai vu le futur du Renault Espace : je n’ai jamais autant voulu un monospace
articles.summary:
Je l’avoue d’emblée, j’ai un faible pour les monospaces, et pour des raisons très pratiques. Pour transporter une famille, ses bagages et son bazar, on n’a jamais fait mieux qu’une boîte bien dessinée, avec un plancher plat et des sièges qu’on déplace à sa guise. Le SUV a tout balayé en vingt ans, l’Espace lui-même s’y est converti en 2023, et j’avais fini par me résigner. Puis je suis tombé sur l’E-Space Concept, dévoilé par Renault le 12 octobre au Mondial de l’Auto de Paris.
Une silhouette qu’on reconnaît à vingt mètres
En arrivant sur le stand, on comprend tout de suite ce qu’on regarde. Le capot court se prolonge dans le pare-brise, d’un seul trait, comme sur le premier Espace de 1984 et son fameux « profil TGV ». La poupe est presque verticale, surmontée d’un becquet qui m’a rappelé les Espace 2 et 3. Autour de moi, des visiteurs de tous âges faisaient le même rapprochement à voix haute, y compris les plus jeunes comme moi, qui n’ont connu l’Espace que sur la banquette arrière de leurs parents.
Vient ensuite le gabarit. Avec 4,70 mètres de long, l’E-Space est à peine plus court que l’Espace actuel (4,72 mètres), mais il est bien plus large (2,02 mètres, soit 18 centimètres de plus) et à peine plus haut (1,67 mètre). En vrai, il paraît trapu, posé, très large. Les roues de 23 pouces repoussées aux quatre coins y sont pour beaucoup. Soyons honnêtes, on ne les reverra sans doute pas sur un modèle de série.
J’ai aussi aimé que Renault ne cède pas au gigantisme : ni calandre…

"SafePay is one of the most active ransomware groups and have affected businesses and critical infrastructure in North America, South America, Europe, and Australia—including at least 600 organizations from multiple critical infrastructure sectors since August 2024," CISA said.

Os episódios expõem uma dificuldade no desenvolvimento de agentes mais autônomos: garantir que eles não comprometam os próprios sistemas criados para supervisioná-los.

Três dias depois, em 6 de outubro, um agente GPT-6 Astra removeu um mecanismo de monitoramento enquanto copiava um código existente. Depois, afirmou incorretamente que não havia realizado a remoção.
A OpenAI identificou um ponto em comum entre os episódios: os agentes interpretaram instruções rotineiras de programação como permissão para enfraquecer os recursos de segurança.
“Em ambos os casos, os agentes avaliaram se os mecanismos de monitoramento deveriam ser mantidos, mas interpretaram instruções rotineiras de programação como permissão para enfraquecê-los”, afirmou a empresa.

articles.title: Cleaning up PFAS
articles.summary:
Cleaning up PFAS
Ridding the world of forever chemicals could address a range of health and environmental and health woes.
Scrubbing Earth of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances—a.k.a. PFAS or forever chemicals—could eliminate a list of woes for people and planet. Used for decades in everything from nonstick pans to firefighting foams, PFAS have been linked to increased risks of fertility challenges, developmental delays, cancer, and reduced immune response. They are known for a strong bond between carbon and fluorine, which the environment struggles to break down.
The sticking points
PFAS are everywhere: They spew from factories and slough off products and into water with normal use. Scientists have found them in everything from human blood to Antarctic snow. One 2022 report found that 89% of the US population had PFAS in excess of two nanograms per milliliter of blood plasma, a common threshold for potential adverse health effects, and 9% of the population had passed the riskier level of 20 nanograms per milliliter.
The PFAS monster is also a moving target. New compounds are still being created and used. There are more than 12,000 of them, and much of the cleanup research focuses on only a small handful.
The progress
Cleansing PFAS-contaminated soil is a project in its infancy, but it is possible to prevent more buildup by pulling the chemicals out of water systems. There are two ways to handle this: trap or destroy. Some scientists have found reverse osmosis—a process that…

Always On VPN replaced the legacy DirectAccess technology and supports domain-joined, non-domain-joined, and Microsoft Entra ID–joined devices running Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server.
It runs in the background and establishes secure tunnels back to the user's corporate network whenever their device connects to the internet.

"When automatic protocol selection or protocol fallback was configured, affected VPN connections could remain stuck in a Connecting state or fail to connect after an initial connection attempt failed," it said. The latest Chrome iteration is now rolling out as versions 156.0.8078.47/.48 for Windows and macOS, and as version 156.0.8078.47 for Linux.

articles.title: Interspecies communication
articles.summary:
Interspecies communication
Decoding how animals communicate could reveal the inner lives of other species—and give humans a window onto how they see the world.
Humans are far from the only species with a gift for gab, and our furry, feathered, and finned friends could have a lot to tell us. Decoding how animals communicate with one another could offer a window into the inner lives of other species and help humans realize that “animals are sentient creatures who think, who have hopes and dreams of their own,” says Con Slobodchikoff, the founder of Zoolingua, a company working on dog-to-human speech.
The sticking points
Teasing all this out is complex. To decipher howls, squeaks, and clicks, researchers must match the creatures making sounds with what’s happening around them. Prairie dogs, for example, utter a different series of yips when a coyote approaches than when a hawk is nearby. It’s painstaking work, especially for difficult-to-observe species, like deep-diving whales or subterranean mole rats.
There are other hurdles. Many animals communicate not just through sound but through visual cues, touch, pheromones, or a combination of signals, some of which might be difficult for us to perceive. And without a multispecies Rosetta stone, it’s hard to know if translations are accurate.
The progress

articles.title: AI sped up coding. Sonar instills confidence with verification.
articles.summary:
AI sped up coding. Sonar instills confidence with verification.
AI coding tools can produce a striking burst of productivity — but the initial surge may not last. A Carnegie Mellon study of public repositories adopting Cursor found a three- to five-fold increase in lines added during the first month, with the gains dissipating after roughly two months. The study, which used SonarQube (Sonar’s core platform) to measure code quality, also found that static analysis warnings rose by 30% and code complexity by 41%. The short-term velocity boost therefore comes with a persistent increase in technical debt.
Tom Howlett, Sonar’s Director of AI Engineering Engagement, tells The New Stack that while coding has sped up, verification, which many teams still rely on manual code review to do, hasn’t kept pace. If developers generate 50 times more code while relying on the same review process, time spent on code review rises and becomes a bottleneck, Howlett tells The New Stack.
There’s another complication. Agents don’t always know how to make the smallest change needed to deliver a feature. Without sufficient context about the codebase, they can make assumptions, generate unnecessary code, and add to technical debt. As Howlett puts it, you end up with more complex, verbose code, which makes the problem worse.

articles.title: Exercise in a pill
articles.summary:
Exercise in a pill
In unraveling the pathways by which movement helps the body, we could develop medicines that offer some of the same benefits, without the workout.
We all know exercise is good for us. It builds muscle, strengthens bones, lowers blood pressure, and boosts mood. By deciphering how movement benefits the body, researchers hope to develop medicines that can offer some of the same perks—without the workout. The idea isn’t to replace exercise but to bring its upsides to people who struggle with frailty, disability, or chronic illness.
The sticking points
It will take a lot of experimentation to untangle the myriad pathways by which exercise promotes health. But IDing the cascade of hormones, enzymes, and other molecules related to physical activity is just the first step. Scientists need to figure out how to turn that knowledge into safe and effective drugs. That’s a tall order: More than 90% of treatments that enter human studies fail.
There are regulatory hurdles too. The FDA approves medications to treat diseases, not to enhance wellness, says Thomas Burris, a pharmacologist at the University of Florida whose work focuses on diseases that respond to exercise, like obesity, type 2 diabetes, and dementia.
The progress
There may never be a pill that delivers all the benefits of exercise, but research could lead to new medicines that mimic some aspects of working out. Scientists have already identified many important exercise-related signals and have even developed…

articles.title: From feral to fiduciary: making AI agents serve your interests
articles.summary:
From feral to fiduciary: making AI agents serve your interests
Tech leaders face a dilemma as they prepare to put AI agents into production. They want the higher productivity and lower costs that AI agents can provide. But they fear unknown risks from AI capabilities that differ from the rest of their software stack. When an agent makes decisions and takes actions on its own, it might be doing its best work. It might also be doing its worst.
As AI agents become more capable, organizations want assurance that their oversight can keep up. How do they strike the right balance between innovation and risk? It comes down to how well they can assess, measure, and maintain trust in their agents. The more trust agents earn, the more autonomy they can be granted.
Trust as a line of credit
Think about the way credit card risk is managed. When you apply for a card, the issuer assesses your credit history and ability to repay before setting a credit limit. Then, once you have your card, payments are subject to real-time authorization and fraud controls. Unusual transactions can trigger additional scrutiny. Paying your card on time may improve your credit score, but it won’t automatically increase your credit limit.
AI agents should be treated similarly.

Nuclear-powered spaceships
A new era of spaceflight could save astronauts time and cut exposure to cosmic radiation as they rocket to Mars—and beyond.
Just before the Artemis II crew began its historic slingshot around the moon this past April, NASA announced plans to build Space Reactor-1 Freedom. SR-1, the first-ever nuclear-reactor-powered interplanetary spacecraft, is meant to fly an uncrewed mission to Mars by the end of 2028, arriving in 2029. A successful mission would herald a new era of more efficient, potentially faster spaceflight—saving astronauts time and cutting their exposure to harmful cosmic radiation as they travel to Mars and beyond. “You wake up to that announcement, and it puts a big smile on your face,” says Simon Middleburgh, co-director of the Nuclear Futures Institute at Bangor University in Wales.

And experts say there aren’t any major technical obstacles to making nuclear space propulsion happen. “I think it’s a very doable technology,” says Philip Metzger, a spaceflight engineering researcher at the Florida Space Institute.“I’m happy to see them finally doing this.”

The approach bridges AWS IAM with Netflix’s internal Metatron PKI, allowing managed compute workloads to authenticate to internal services without manually injecting credentials.
Dhruv Pratap, Big Data Platform Engineer at Netflix, described the design in a LinkedIn post as
On infrastructure you build yourself, you can bootstrap your own identity however you like.
Netflix operates two identity systems. AWS provides managed workloads with an IAM execution role, while internal services use Metatron, a private PKI that issues short-lived X.509 certificates for mutual TLS. Netflix also uses Data Projects as the ownership and identity boundary for data access. A Spark job running on EMR therefore needs to establish that its AWS identity corresponds to the internal identity associated with its Data Project.
The design maps each Data Project to a dedicated IAM role. Because Netflix expects Data Projects to reach the tens of thousands, these roles are deterministically distributed across a pool of dedicated AWS accounts rather than concentrated in one account.

articles.title: ‘Context Bombs’ Cut AI Attack Success by Misleading Agents With Fake Targets

Just as landmines are used to destroy or slow an advancing army, Tracebit has developed AI ‘context bombs’ that are planted in the battlefield. Each bomb comprises crafted and hidden prompts that are automatically ingested by the attacking AI when it crawls the target. These new prompts interfere with the original, possibly malign, purpose of the attacking agent.
Tracebit’s new research (Making attacking agents pay’) extends earlier research that used different context bombs to trigger guardrails. It now focuses on misdirecting and entrapping the agents with fake targets and deceptively complex problems. To achieve this, Tracebit developed nine new context techniques (ingested fake prompts) that stopped all GPT 5.6 Cyber, Kimi K3, Qwen 3.8 Max, and DeepSeek V4 Pro attacks. The same bombs also worked against Frontier Models, cutting GPT-6 Astra’s successes by 54% and nearly quadrupling its bill per attack. The effect against Claude Opus 5 was even more obvious: attack success was cut by 91%.
The single most effective of the nine prompt bombs was a fake pen testing report. It presented itself as a recent assessment, labeled real attack paths as canaries, and described decoys as valuable targets that had already been exploited. "We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs," the PHP security team said.
Both flaws stem from the same underlying problem: PHP can leave its memory in a corrupted state when a request ends abnormally, and both can be exploited to achieve remote code execution.
CVE-2026-109618 can be used to gain remote code execution as the web worker account by exploiting a chain of weaknesses that trigger out-of-memory corruption, while the CVE-2026-109619 stale global state vulnerability enables unauthenticated heap use-after-free, memory disclosure, and remote code execution with the web worker's privileges.
Admins should install PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35 as soon as possible on servers running PHP 8.x and migrate to a fixed release if they're running PHP 7 or earlier.

articles.title: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise
articles.summary:
Private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate Certificate Authority (CA) certificates have been compromised, making it trivial for attackers to forge certificates that would be trusted by unpatched roots of trust. Six of the impacted certificates were for Transport Layer Security (TLS) and trusted by the Apple, Chrome, Microsoft and Mozilla root programs. The other two certificates were for codesigning and trusted by Microsoft. Browsers were able to block the affected intermediate CAs using their background revocation blocklists, but most other software relying on web public key infrastructure (PKI) lacks any mechanism to filter intermediate CAs. In order to defend against rogue certificates from the compromised intermediate CAs many projects have chosen to remove the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 from their roots of trust. That removal is causing collateral damage for all legitimate certificates previously issued by CAs chained to that root.
Forged certificates can potentially be used to impersonate sites and services as part of a man in the middle (MITM) attack. The underlying problem is that there are hundreds of CAs in a typical root CA bundle, and thousands of intermediate CAs that inherit trust. Any one of those CAs can create a legitimate looking certificate for any domain. The chain of trust is only broken if the trust anchors are updated to reflect the compromise. This leaves any unpatched system vulnerable.

articles.title: Youtuber construye refrigerador que utiliza fuego y sal para enfriar sin electricidad
articles.summary:
Un canal de YouTube dedicado a la metalurgia y la ingeniería casera construyó un refrigerador que funciona con fuego, agua y sal de carretera, sin depender de un compresor eléctrico convencional. El proyecto, desarrollado por Greenhill Forge, logró enfriar una sección del dispositivo hasta los 5 °C (41 °F) mientras la temperatura ambiente rondaba los 16 °C (61 °F), un resultado que el propio canal documentó en video.
La propuesta retoma un principio de ingeniería centenario con una aplicación actual: la posibilidad de generar frío en lugares donde la electricidad es escasa o poco confiable.
El principio detrás del sistema: absorción refrigerante
El dispositivo se basa en la refrigeración por absorción, una técnica que existe desde hace más de un siglo y que prescinde del compresor eléctrico para hacer circular el refrigerante. En su lugar, utiliza calor para impulsar una reacción química que produce el efecto de enfriamiento.
El diseño de Greenhill Forge se compone de dos secciones principales: un generador y un absorbedor. El generador contiene una solución de cloruro de calcio y agua destilada. Cuando el fuego calienta esa mezcla, el vapor de agua se separa de la solución y viaja a través de una tubería hasta un condensador, donde se enfría y vuelve a su estado líquido.

Bitcoin for treasury, stablecoins for payments. That rule fits most of what a business does with either asset, and it fails in two places. It treats Bitcoin’s volatility as a one-way risk, and it treats a stablecoin as a permanent hedge against the naira.

|  | Bitcoin | Fiat-backed stablecoin (USDT, USDC) |

| Accountability | No issuer, rules enforced by the network | Named issuer, reserves, redemption terms |

Price stability, and what “stable” costs

articles.title: OpenAI descubre que un agente de ChatGPT desactivó su propio sistema de seguridad y mintió

OpenAI abrió una investigación para encontrar por qué una IA desactivó parte de sus sistemas de supervisión. La compañía publicó un informe en el que describe dos incidentes ocurridos durante pruebas internas de sus modelos de lenguaje, en donde un agente de GPT-6 Astra debilitó los mecanismos de monitoreo y mintió sobre su comportamiento.
En una publicación de su blog de seguridad, la compañía mencionó que ambos casos involucraron agentes de IA especializados en programación. Si bien las situaciones fueron diferentes, los dos modelos modificaron o desactivaron elementos de supervisión de seguridad mientras intentaban completar una tarea legítima.
El primero de ellos ocurrió durante la reparación de una herramienta de evaluación interna, cuando un investigador le pidió al agente de GPT-6.1 Sol que recopilara información desde Slack, pero sin enviar mensajes a los usuarios. Al llevar a cabo la tarea, el sistema de monitoreo envió una notificación de seguridad, lo que provocó que el modelo reinterpretara la instrucción y anulara estas alertas automáticas.
OpenAI menciona que el agente modificó la configuración y activó opciones que impedían el envío de notificaciones de seguridad. La IA también vació las listas de destinatarios de los avisos, lo que provocó que las personas responsables no recibieran estas alertas. El agente justificó la medida diciendo que la instrucción original era no enviar mensajes de Slack al equipo de OpenAI.

articles.title: Why you don't need an audiophile headset for gaming — comfort, convenience, and a good mic win over pure audio fidelity
articles.summary:
Why you don't need an audiophile headset for gaming — comfort, convenience, and a good mic win over pure audio fidelity
Audiophile headsets are all about audio fidelity — but that's not really what most gamers are looking for.
"Best gaming headset for audiophiles" is one of the categories on our list of best gaming headsets, and it's easy to look at that and wonder if you shouldn't be looking at just audiophile headsets to begin with. Headsets are mainly about audio, after all, and it does seem to logically follow that audiophile headsets would have the best audio (I mean, it's in the name).
Well, not so fast.
Headsets are mainly about audio, but that doesn't mean that the "objectively" best-sounding headset by audiophile standards translates to the best-sounding headset by gaming standards. Nor does it mean that you should choose your gaming headset based on audio quality at the expense of everything else.
Audiophile headsets, including headphones, are primarily designed around one thing: audio fidelity. In other words, they're designed and tuned to reproduce audio exactly as it was recorded, which is exactly as the artist heard it when they were recording it, and is therefore exactly as the artist intended for it to be heard. This doesn't necessarily mean it's going to sound amazing to everyone. In fact, to many people it will probably sound somewhat underwhelming, but it's really the only objective way we have of measuring what makes audio "good," since how something sound…

articles.title: Stop choosing the wrong Agentic AI use cases
articles.summary:
Stop choosing the wrong Agentic AI use cases
Choose agentic AI use cases by measurable business value
Psychologist Abraham Maslow once warned: “It is tempting, if the only tool you have is a hammer, to treat everything as if it were a nail.” Agentic AI is becoming the enterprise version of that hammer.
Once people understand what agentic AI can do, the list of possible use cases grows quickly.
VP of AI transformation at Atos.
While that enthusiasm should be applauded, it can lead to strategies that are back to front “If AI is the answer, what’s the question?” By the time it comes to looking at results and whether the investment in AI has been fruitful, it’s hard to identify what’s been achieved and why achieving it was important in the first place.
Start with the value, not the agent
In the rush that followed ChatGPT, many organizations deployed AI tools to their workforces at large with no defined value or end goal. People started working differently almost immediately, but with no baseline captured, there was no way to know what had actually improved. Who knows how long it takes to write a coherent email and who knows what time is saved by having ChatGPT rephrase it for you!
This is what McKinsey calls the “gen AI paradox”. Its 2025 survey found just 39% of organizations reported any enterprise-level financial impact from their AI investment, despite mass adoption.

Google has announced new Chrome protections against scams and social engineering, including new site warnings, server-side Gemini analysis, and detection of ClickFix commands.
The Gemini and ClickFix protections are part of Enhanced Protection, the Safe Browsing mode Google introduced in 2020. Last year, the company said more than 1 billion Chrome users had turned it on.
Google claims Enhanced Protection makes users “ten times safer” than Standard Protection against phishing, social engineering, notification abuse, and other scams. The metric is based on how many safety warnings, on average, each group of users receives.
Chrome’s Safe Browsing site warnings now come in two levels, mirroring a model previously applied to file downloads. When Safe Browsing is highly confident a page is malicious, users still get the full-page red ‘dangerous site’ warning.
The new ‘suspicious site’ level covers lower-confidence verdicts. It flags pages that use deceptive tactics typical of known malicious sites. Because these warnings have their own design, Google says it can safely display more of them.
Gemini-powered scam detection has also moved to Google’s servers. The on-device version launched last year focused on tech support scams and was limited to Enhanced Protection users on supported devices.

Building AI in India? Privacy is now a valuation issue: Shivaarti Bajaj
At TechSparks 2026, Shivaarti Bajaj of RSD Bajaj Global Law Firm explains why consent, data mapping, and breach readiness under India’s DPDP Act now shape how investors value AI and data-driven startups.
As India’s startups race to build AI-first products, the way they handle personal data could decide what those companies are eventually worth.
Speaking at TechSparks 2026, YourStory’s annual flagship summit, Shivaarti Bajaj, Founding Managing Partner of RSD Bajaj Global Law Firm, argued that privacy can no longer be an afterthought. Founders, she said, are not just shipping products but creating assets: assets that can be valued, bought, sold, devalued, or even taken away if they are not built and complied with correctly.
“When we are creating products, we are creating companies, an asset,” Bajaj said.
Intellectual property remains the first line of defence. Trademarks protect the brands that D2C companies are building, patents matter for deep tech innovation, and copyrights and design protection cover creators, semiconductors, and IoT hardware. But Bajaj noted that IP law in India is well established. The newer and less understood risk lies in the data sets companies collect and create.

eMudhra faces scrutiny after weak certificate keys raise web security concerns
Eight weak intermediate certificate keys have prompted browser safeguards and questions over eMudhra’s controls, although the company said customer data and Indian eSign services remain unaffected.
Eight intermediate certificate authority keys linked to eMudhra’s global website-security business were found to be dangerously weak, raising concerns about the systems that browsers use to establish trust online.
The flaw could have enabled attackers to create fraudulent HTTPS certificates and impersonate legitimate websites. The keys were generated on April 30, 2025, but the weakness remained undetected for about 18 months, according to eMudhra’s statement on October 21, 2026.
A certificate authority (CA) verifies identities and issues digital certificates. Intermediate authorities operate under a root certificate trusted by browsers and operating systems.
eMudhra said a key-wrap/unwrap step during its key-generation procedure produced a second, weak set of keys, which were subsequently published to browser root stores. Although the company added its root private key was not compromised, browser operators have withdrawn trust from the associated emSign ECC Root CA - G3 as a precaution.

Betroffen ist die weit verbreitete Programmiersprache PHP, auf der ein Großteil des gesamten Internets basiert – von einfachen Blogs über große Nachrichtenportale bis hin zu komplexen Onlineshops und Content-Management-Systemen wie WordPress.
Wie unter anderem das IT-Sicherheitsunternehmen Huntress, das Computer Emergency Response Team des Bundes (CERT) sowie das offizielle PHP-Sicherheitsteam berichten, handelt es sich um eine akute Notfallsituation, die Betreiber von Internetseiten in aller Welt zu schnellem Handeln zwingt.
Gefährlicher Fehler ermöglicht vollständige Übernahme
Unter dem Namen PHP2Shell warnen Sicherheitsexperten vor gleich zwei kritischen Schwachstellen im Kern der Programmiersprache, die unter den offiziellen Registriernummern CVE-2026-109618 und CVE-2026-109619 geführt werden. Das Gefahrenpotenzial dieser Lücken ist demnach extrem hoch: Kriminelle Akteure können die Schwachstelle ausnutzen, um aus der Ferne eigenen Schadcode auf den betroffenen Servern auszuführen.
In der Praxis ermöglicht dies Angreifern, die vollständige Kontrolle über eine Website zu übernehmen, sensible Kundendaten abzugreifen oder die Infrastruktur für weitere Cyberattacken zu missbrauchen.

Mais fort heureusement, des correctifs étaient promis pour le mercredi 21 octobre en milieu d’après-midi.
Ces patchs viennent d’être publiés, en urgence, ce qui a donné lieu à quatre nouvelles versions de son langage : PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 et 8.2.35.
Il est capital de mettre à jour, dès que possible, sa version de PHP. Il faut en effet avoir conscience que PHP est derrière plus de 70 % des sites dont on connaît le langage côté serveur, à commencer par tous les sites WordPress.
D’après l’avis de sécurité publié par PHP, toutes les installations qui servent des pages web sont exposées, y compris avec PHP-FPM ou FrankenPHP. Le risque est maximal avec mod_php, le module qui intègre PHP directement au serveur Apache. Dans ce cas, une requête anonyme suffit à déclencher l’attaque avant même que le code du site s’exécute.
PHP donne bien quelques réglages de secours, mais prévient qu’ils ne rendent pas un serveur sûr. Surtout, PHP 8.1 et les versions plus anciennes ne reçoivent plus de mises à jour officielles. Pour les versions 7.4, 8.0 et 8.1, l’équipe a seulement mis en ligne des correctifs minimaux, qu’il faut compiler soi-même.

Dans le code des pages de support de WhatsApp, l'équipe y avait glissé des consignes demandant au chatbot de ne pas conseiller aux utilisateurs de contacter une autorité de protection des données.
C'est la société Redact, spécialisée dans la suppression de données personnelles, qui a découvert ces instructions en début de mois. De son côté, WhatsApp parle d'un bug et assure que ces textes s'adressaient à son chatbot, pas aux utilisateurs.
Pour le chatbot de WhatsApp, pas question de parler du régulateur
Ces textes ne s'affichaient pas à l'écran. Ils étaient glissés dans le code source des pages, que n'importe qui peut afficher depuis son navigateur. Redact a passé en revue les 545 pages liées au centre d'aide et a trouvé 102 blocs d'instructions sur 80 d'entre elles. La plupart sont classiques et le chatbot est invité à expliquer un terme, renvoyer vers une autre page, ou présenter des offres payantes.
Mais il y a deux blocs qui posent problème. Le premier concerne la suppression d'un compte WhatsApp, et plus particulièrement, lorsque le téléphone sur lequel la messagerie a été utilisée a été perdu ou volé.
Le chatbot est censé expliquer que les comptes WhatsApp désactivés sont effacés au bout de 30 jours et les comptes inactifs le sont au bout de 120 jours. C'est en tout cas ce qui est retourné à l'internaute. Mais la filiale de Meta avait également d'autres consignes dans le code de la page. A OpenAI diz que você não perde as mensagens caso erre o PIN, mas, caso precise resetá-lo, todas essas conversas serão apagadas. Uma saída é recorrer à biometria do seu celular no app, por exemplo.

AMD has also joined the UXL Foundation as a steering member.
Intel and AMD are integrating their CPU optimizations for PyTorch into a unified library, offering tuning for both AMD and Intel chips through the oneDNN library. AMD has maintained a downstream version of oneDNN called ZenDNN, which is now moving into the open-source oneDNN, published by the UXL Foundation and driven by Intel. AMD also announced it's joining the UXL Foundation as a "steering member," which "influences the future of the UXL Foundation" in exchange for a contribution of $20,000 per year.
AMD says the move to unify these efforts under oneDNN was recommended by the x86 Ecosystem Advisory Group (EAG), which is a joint initiative that primarily exists between Intel and AMD and was established in 2024. The two companies have collaborated through the EAG previously, such as with the ACE extensions for x86 that we learned about earlier this year.
The oneDNN backend is used for CPU inference, and it's built to accelerate that workload for the latest Intel (and now AMD) chips in frameworks like PyTorch. When oneDNN was added to PyTorch as a backend in late 2023, it showed a 1.24x improvement with the Float32 data type, and 2.21x for the BFloat16 data type.

articles.title: Panne Orange : l’astuce simple pour retrouver appels et SMS sur votre smartphone, nous l’avons testée
articles.summary:
Si, comme moi, vous êtes toujours privé de réseau Orange ou Sosh, cette astuce peut vous intéresser. Elle ne va pas faire revenir votre réseau comme par magie, mais elle permet au moins de pouvoir téléphoner et envoyer des SMS… surtout si vous êtes sous Android.
Il semblerait que la panne qui affecte l’opérateur touche les réseaux 4G et 5G d’Orange, la 3G restant épargnée. La solution, repérée par Le Parisien, consiste donc à forcer son smartphone à utiliser la 3G plutôt que la 4G ou la 5G. Je l’ai testé sur différents modèles de smartphones, et elle m’a permis de d’envoyer et recevoir des SMS ainsi que des appels. En revanche, il ne m’a pas été possible de retrouver l’accès à Internet à l’heure de ces lignes.
Comment passer en 3G sur Android ?
Rendez-vous dans les paramètres, puis dans « Réseau et Internet » ou « Connexions » selon votre modèle. Ouvrez les réglages du réseau mobile, puis « Type de réseau préféré » ou « Mode réseau », et choisissez la 3G (parfois appelée « 3G uniquement » ou « WCDMA »).
Les manipulations, ainsi que les intitulés, peuvent très légèrement varier en fonction de la marque de votre smartphone, et certains modèles récents ne proposent plus cette option.

Malheureusement, la manipulation se complique sur iPhone puisque les modèles récents et à jour ne proposent plus de forcer la connectivité 3G. Si vous voulez quand même vérifier ce qu’il est possible de faire, le choix du réseau se fait dans Réglages, Données cellulaires, Options, pu…

articles.title: AI promises productivity, but for managers, it's mostly a headache for now | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Companies are giving employees AI tools to make them more productive, but the tools appear to be creating new problems for their managers.
More than half of senior leaders say they find it harder to evaluate employees’ work after adopting AI, according to a Nielsen survey of 1,700 directors and senior managers across seven countries, commissioned by work-management company Monday.com. The reason is that much of employees’ output now arrives polished in the manager’s inbox, making it hard to tell how much came from the employee and how much from AI. As a result, nearly half of managers say they spend more time reviewing and guiding their teams’ output than they used to.
That’s not to say managers are unhappy about AI. Quite the opposite, in fact: 94% of the managers polled said they were excited to improve work using AI, and many are confident they know where to use it to get the most value. Michal Miller Levi, head of market research and customer insights at Monday.com, compared the enthusiasm to the early days of the internet in the 2000s, saying people see a similar kind of “magic” to AI.
But the problem, she told TechCrunch, is simply that AI is developing faster than companies can adapt. “AI works very well for [managers] individually, but they also have a different role as managers. They need to drive the organization as well … Their struggle is [due to] the fact that AI is just moving faster than the organizational processes,” Levi said.

articles.title: PHP warns it plans to release 2 emergency patches imminently

Website admins, brace yourselves. Fixes for what are believed to be uncommonly severe vulnerabilities are scheduled to drop in a little more than 12 hours for PHP, a programming language that powers websites and Web applications everywhere.
PHP maintainers said Monday that they planned to release patches for two vulnerabilities, both with severity ratings of 9.2 out of a possible 10.
Waiting for PHP2Shell
“All PHP users are encouraged to prepare now so they can upgrade as soon as the release is available,” the advisory stated. “We reserve the right to release earlier should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild.”
The maintainers published the advisory following the leaking of purported details, which have yet to be confirmed. The report showed a video of an exploit tool dubbed PHP2Shell executing code on webservers running:
- WordPress 7.1.3
- MediaWiki 1.46.2
- phpBB 3.3.17
- Magento 2.4.9
- Joomla 6.2.0
- Laravel 13.36.0
- Laravel 8.83.29
- Symphony 8.1.9
- Drupal 11.4.10
- WHMCS 9.0.9
All of the above use PHP. A video depicting the tool has been reposted here.
Attempts to locate the unconfirmed report were unsuccessful, but security firm watchTowr said it claimed to affect every PHP version from PHP 5, released in 2004, onward. The security firm went on to say it has confirmed that the vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are real.

articles.title: Meta suspends Muse sharing after sensitive documents turn up in shared chats
articles.summary:
What we know so far: Meta has paused the conversation-sharing feature in its Muse AI assistant after security researchers discovered thousands of links in public DNS records. Some of the links exposed sensitive business documents and personal financial information that anyone could access without logging in. Researchers at security firm Claroc traced the exposure to the way Muse generated its web addresses.
Each shared conversation had a hostname containing a descriptive title and a random identifier. Both could appear in searchable DNS records, giving researchers the information they needed to reconstruct the link and open the page.
"People have the ability to share specific Muse artifacts, which creates a page that can be accessed by those with the link," Muse spokesperson Tracy Clayton said in a statement to The Verge. "However, we've paused this functionality while we review this report and consider changes to how these links can be discovered."
Sharing tools commonly rely on long, random strings in their URLs to prevent outsiders from guessing an address. Muse used random identifiers that Claroc said were long enough to resist guessing. The weakness lay in where Muse placed them: in the hostname, alongside a title describing the conversation.

The drive answers NFS requests itself, but samples won’t reach partners until Q3 2027.
SSD controller designer FADU’s new File-Semantic SSD (FS-SSD) was announced at the 2026 OCP Global Summit. The new device promises to move the file system into the SSD itself. As detailed in a white paper, this enables GPUs, DPUs, and NICs to open and read files with “no host filesystem, no block layer, and no storage-server CPU in the path.” FADU told Tom’s Hardware Premium it expects partner samples by Q3 2027.
FADU is a Seoul, South Korea-based fabless SSD controller designer. Its FS-SSD technology is designed to handle and improve the control path, as the data path side moved to accelerators years ago. FADU’s measurements show that the file system, plus block layers, can consume about 30% of CPU cycles in a GPUDirect Storage (GDS) random-read workload. It notes that bypass options give up the files, and the company claims its solution promises the best of both worlds.
In FADU’s own preliminary Network File System (NFS) over NVMe test, on a drive built on its FC6161 Gen6 controller in a PCIe 5.0 host, remote file throughput held steady as the server downshifted from what FADU labels 16 cores to just one, maintaining about 460,000 ops/s.

articles.title: Celebrities don't sell, the product does: Ananth Narayanan on what makes a D2C brand last

Celebrities don't sell, the product does: Ananth Narayanan on what makes a D2C brand last
At TechSparks 2026, the BRND.ME founder says the growth-hack era is over and the brands that survive will be built on product love, cash flows and global ambition.
The froth has gone out of D2C, and brands that want to last will have to earn it slowly. That was the message from Ananth Narayanan, Founder and CEO of BRND.ME, at the 17th edition of YourStory's TechSparks.
In a fireside chat with Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO of YourStory and The Bharat Project, Narayanan said the shift towards profitable businesses began two to three years ago. "Without product-market fit, just scaling, which a lot of D2C brands used to do, I don't think is valued anymore," he said. "You need real cash flows, you need real product love, which is very hard."
There is no shortcut, he added, "I don't think there is a get-rich-quick on brand building." In his experience a brand takes seven to 15 years to earn real loyalty and cohorts that last five or ten years. Patient capital is becoming easier to find, he said, through FMCG majors such as Unilever and P&G buying D2C brands, and through a coming wave of IPOs. Founders can help themselves by being frugal. "Most of the large FMCG businesses never took any money. Is it possible for D2C to do the same? I think the answer is yes. It's hard. It's very unsexy."
Think global from day one
Narayanan believes India's next big brands will be built for overseas shoppers…

I have conflicting feelings about Stranger Than Heaven.
After playing around three hours of the game in New York City earlier this month, I find a lot to like and also be apprehensive about. On the one hand, I see a lot of promise in the sprawling narrative and world that developer RGG Studio is building here. But on the other hand, some of the broader gameplay mechanics, as well as specific creative decisions, aren’t working for me so far.
But first, the positives. In terms of pure ambition, the story hook of Stranger Than Heaven is certainly one of the most impressive I’ve seen in a while. In 1915, Japanese-American orphan Makoto Daito stows away on a ship to Japan in search of a better life, and from there, the game follows him on a 50-year journey across four additional time periods. It’s also a standalone prequel to RGG’s Like a Dragon series, chronicling Makoto’s formation of the yakuza organization Tojo Clan that features prominently in those other games.
Allowing you to play through this progression, rather than simply watch it unfold, definitely holds a great deal of potential. And on a personal level, I love that Makoto is half-white, half-Japanese. As someone who is also biracial, it’s a bummer that we don’t often see such characters in media, so I appreciate how this identity serves as the backbone of Makoto’s story. Le 15 octobre 2026, la Cour de justice de l’Union européenne (CJUE) a fini par trancher sur la question des remboursements accordés aux victimes d’arnaques en ligne. La plus haute juridiction de l’Union européenne a statué qu’une banque doit rembourser un paiement « non autorisé », même si le client a commis une « négligence grave ».
La banque peut complètement s’abstenir de rembourser son client dans un seul cas bien particulier. Si la banque soupçonne une fraude du client lui-même, elle peut refuser le remboursement. Si elle a « des motifs raisonnables de soupçonner une fraude de la part du client lui-même », la banque n’a fort logiquement pas l’obligation de rembourser l’utilisateur. Par ailleurs, la banque peut récupérer la somme remboursée ultérieurement si elle prouve que le client a commis une négligence grave, mettant en danger ses avoirs. En clair, la banque doit d’abord verser de l’argent à son client, avant de tenter de prouver qu’une négligence a eu lieu.
Sur le papier, ce changement est une excellente nouvelle pour les clients et les victimes. Ceux-ci ne risquent plus de se retrouver sans le sou à la suite d’une escroquerie. En pratique, les banques ne sont pas prêtes à changer leur fusil d’épaule, et vont tout faire pour éviter d’avoir à vous rembourser.

articles.title: Placer une pièce de monnaie sur son routeur Wi-Fi : pourquoi et à quoi ça sert
articles.summary:
Placer une pièce de monnaie sur son routeur Wi-Fi : pourquoi et à quoi ça sert
L'astuce fait le tour des réseaux sociaux : poser une pièce, ou un bout d'aluminium, sur sa box internet améliorerait la connexion. La réalité physique est tout autre. Non seulement le métal ne renforce pas le signal, mais il peut le dégrader et faire surchauffer l'appareil. Voici ce qui marche vraiment.
C'est une astuce de grand-mère version numérique qui revient régulièrement sur YouTube : poser délicatement une simple pièce de deux euros sur le dessus de sa box internet permettrait d'obtenir enfin un réseau fluide et sans coupures. Entre démonstrations convaincantes et commentaires enthousiastes, la promesse est séduisante. Le geste est si simple et gratuit qu'on serait tenté de l'essayer sur-le-champ. C'est pourtant là que se niche le piège de ces recettes miracles qui circulent en ligne.
Une croyance séduisante mais sans fondement
L'idée paraît presque logique. Le métal réfléchit les ondes, alors une pièce posée sur la box redirigerait le signal Wi-Fi et étendrait sa portée. articles.title: AMD brings official Ryzen overclocking to Linux with AOD driver support — no official app, but third-party options should arrive soon
articles.summary:
AMD brings official Ryzen overclocking to Linux with AOD driver support — no official app, but third-party options should arrive soon
This is a major milestone for improving the DIY tuning experience on Linux.
While Windows overclockers have spent years lazily sliding UI controls to adjust frequency curves and tweak voltages inside Ryzen Master, Linux users have largely had to treat their CPU tuning like an archaeological dig into the opaque veil of UEFI/BIOS firmware. Well, rejoice, Linux users, as AMD has officially published a fresh set of patches for the Linux kernel introducing AOD (AMD Overclocking Driver) support for Ryzen processors, Phoronix reports.
Instead of forcing developers to reverse-engineer closed-source firmware hooks or rely on messy, machine-specific ACPI workarounds, this new kernel driver is a direct pipeline to AMD's platform adjustments. By exposing core tuning capabilities straight through the standard sysfs interface, AMD is laying down an official, upstreamed foundation for software-level CPU management.
Right out of the gate, the driver handles platform-level SMT toggling, memory clock visibility, and power tunables. That's right: you can now toggle Simultaneous Multithreading (SMT) dynamically through this driver interface. That works through the CPU hotplugging mechanism and acts as a clean alternative to passing the old 'nosmt' boot parameter to the kernel. The new driver also allows real-time monitoring of memory clocks, and initial power cont…
